discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (moiré quantum materials)

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

nominees.name: Rafi Bistritzer
nominees.affiliation: Tel Aviv University / Applied Materials, Israel

subfield: Condensed matter physics: two-dimensional and moiré quantum materials
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that at a 'magic' twist angle near 1.1 degrees, interlayer tunnelling in bilayer graphene makes the Dirac velocity vanish and produces nearly flat electronic bands. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group confirmed this in experiment, finding correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene. Together these works showed that rotation between atomic layers can serve as a new control knob, opening the field of moiré quantum materials. In these tunable, gate-controlled platforms, strong correlations, superconductivity, orbital magnetism and quantum anomalous and fractional Chern insulators can all be explored in a single device. Hundreds of groups worldwide have adopted the platform, including those of us doing spectroscopy and nano-imaging. The work has changed how physicists design and study correlated electrons. It realises the idea of programmable quantum matter and has lasting conceptual impact.
